turns.content: Dan was born on April 6 in a perfect-square year between 1300 and 1400, and Steve was born on April 6 in a perfect-square year between 1400 and 1500. Determine their birth years.
Let `Y` be a year in which both are alive. Since the date is April 7, write Dan's and Steve's ages in terms of `Y` and their birth years.
If both ages are perfect squares, derive the equation relating those squares and determine the fixed difference between Dan's and Steve's ages.
Each man lived for 110 years. List the positive perfect-square ages that can occur within that lifespan.
Use the fixed age difference to identify the only possible pair of square ages, and assign the larger age to the older man.
A prominent historian asserts that Steve, not Dan, was the older man. Use that ordering when assigning the two square ages, without revisiting the birth-year calculation.
Determine that calendar year and confirm that both men were still alive on April 7.
